title: Decimals & Rounding
bank_verdict: All 20 stored solutions fresh-solved and confirmed correct (bronze 8, silver 7, gold 5). No wrong answers, no degenerate/non-calculator-messy problems, no duplicate solutions within any tier. No repairs needed.

guided_added.method_card: slimmed to 4 steps + <=140-word content; removed the em dash in the old content ('without rounding — simply remove')

misconception_notes: All misconceptions converted from the old {check,message,pattern} shape to {pattern,message,expect}. 5 rounding misconceptions (bronze[1] 6.845->2dp, bronze[5] 7.996->2dp, silver[0] 0.06472->2sf, silver[2] 0.8097->3sf, gold[4] truncation bound) have expect:null: their natural wrong value sits within the validator's 0.011 numeric tolerance of the correct answer, so the harness cannot separate it; message retained as documentation, fires never (never false-diagnoses). Remaining 15 expects derived by committing the error and all differ from the correct answer.
opener_concept: Till rounding: a card machine that only charges whole pounds. £6.85 -> £7, £6.40 -> £6. Reveal names it as rounding to the nearest whole number (check if the part after the point passes halfway), the same move used for decimal places and significant figures.
figures_note: None. Decimals & rounding is purely numeric/textual; a GCSE exam prints no figure for these items (rounding, truncation, decimal arithmetic, estimation). Exam-realism test => no SVG/chart warranted.
completion_boundaries: Every bank walk tags the finishing phase with phase:'substitute' after the set-up move (locating the target place / rounding each factor to 1 s.f. / clearing decimals), leaving >=2 live boxes for the student to finish and land on the stored solution.
preservation: related_videos, topic_links, worked_examples preserved byte-for-byte vs pre-edit live. Only practice_data column patched; solutions unchanged in all tiers.
